title: Hybrid kernel stitcher for gradual FlashAttention v3 rollout with replay evaluation
creator: Lena Morales
description: Background: FlashAttention v3 brings faster kernels for many shapes but increases memory fragmentation and occasionally regresses tail-latency during mixed v2/v3 rollouts. Existing approaches either do coarse model-wide routing or full-version pinning, both of which either sacrifice throughput or delay rollout. Proposal: implement a lightweight 'hybrid kernel stitcher' in the runtime that can do per-layer/per-step kernel selection and stitch KV cache outputs when the kernel family switches mid-context. The stitcher will: 1) maintain compatibility invariants for KV layout when switching between v2 and v3 kernels; 2) orchestrate a short synchronous handoff window where the decoder continues while background warmup populates the alternative kernel's workspace; 3) expose an opt-in canary with replay-eval to detect quality/latency regressions before full rollout; 4) provide telemetry and automated rollback triggers based on token-latency percentiles and failure rates.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime implements stitcher that can switch kernel families mid-context and preserve decoding correctness (no hallucinated tokens or KV corruption), validated by unit tests and fuzzed KV layouts.
End-to-end benchmarks show stitcher adds <6ms median extra latency and does not increase p99 by >5% for our 2 largest long-context models when performing an on-the-fly v2->v3 handoff.
Replay-eval harness can rerun a 5k prompt set against both legacy routing and stitcher-enabled routing and produce a diff report (token-level BLEU-like and perplexity delta) automatically.
Canary rollout plan exists in the console with thresholds (p95 latency increase >7% OR regen failure rate >0.3%) that automatically disable stitcher for that model/region.
Design doc and security checklist reviewed by Runtime and Applied ML teams and linked in ticket comments.
notes: This ticket purposely avoids wholesale flashattn-v3 defaulting; stitcher is an incremental safety layer to enable gradual migration. Watch GPU memory fragmentation metrics closely during canary.
comments: 2026-01-15 Lena Morales: Initial triage - observed intermittent p99 regressions in v3 canaries on A100-80GB under bursty prefill workloads. Created design spike to explore a mid-context handoff instead of a full restart.

2026-01-20 Ravi Patel: Spike results - small prototype can redirect layer 6..11 to v3 kernels mid-decoding and KV shapes match when we remap strides; however workspace allocation timing caused a 12ms median hop in microbenchmarks. Will prototype background warmup to hide cost.

2026-01-25 Marco Díaz (Applied ML): Replay-eval dataset curated (5k prompts, 300 long-history chats). Proposed metric suite: token-level edit distance, repeated-token rate, and loss delta. Attached confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Hybrid+Stitcher+Design
2026-01-29 Design review: feedback - ensure API surfaces are opt-in and clearly labeled in console. UX team requested an observable 'handoff phase' timeline in request traces.

2026-02-02 Ravi Patel: Built canary branch PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8427 - implements stitcher core and background warmup task. Microbenchmarks (A100) show handoff median overhead now 5.1ms, p99 overhead 9.4ms for synthetic prefill workload. See PR benchmarks folder.

2026-02-04 QA: Canary run in us-west-2 for model 'rw-medium-long' for 6 hours. Observed small quality delta: 0.15% token edit distance increase and 0.2% increase in perplexity on replay-eval set. Latency p95 increased 3.8%. No correctness failures reported. Will expand to europe region next.

2026-02-06 Ravi Patel: Raising to In Progress - follow-ups: persistent memory fragmentation telemetry, finer-grained eviction metrics, and a stress test with mixed quantized/FP16 model variants. Filed follow-up tickets (ENG-601122 for telemetry, ENG-601130 for stress harness).
